sanskrit: rakṣitāsmīti coktaṃ te pratijñā cānṛtā tava brāhmaṇasvasya cādānaṃ trividhas te vyatikramaḥ
english: "'I shall be protected'—so it was promised you, yet your pledge proved false; and you took what belonged to a brāhmaṇa: thus your transgression is threefold."

sanskrit: pūrvaṃ kṛcchraṃ cariṣye 'haṃ paścāc chubham iti prabho dharmarājaṃ bruvann evaṃ patito 'smi mahītale
english: "'First I shall undergo the hardship, and the bliss thereafter'—O lord, even as I was saying this to the King of Dharma, I fell upon the surface of the earth."

sanskrit: aśrauṣaṃ pracyutaś cāhaṃ yamasyoccaiḥ prabhāṣataḥ vāsudevaḥ samuddhartā bhavitā te janārdanaḥ
english: "And as I was tumbling down I heard Yama proclaiming aloud: 'Vāsudeva, Janārdana, shall be your deliverer.'"

sanskrit: pūrṇe varṣasahasrānte kṣīṇe karmaṇi duṣkṛte prāpsyase śāśvatāṃl lokāñ jitān svenaiva karmaṇā
english: "'When a full thousand years are ended and your evil deed is exhausted, you shall attain the eternal worlds, won by your own action.'"

sanskrit: kūpe ''tmānam adhaḥśīrṣam apaśyaṃ patitaṃ ca ha tiryagyonim anuprāptaṃ na tu mām ajahāt smṛtiḥ
english: "I beheld myself fallen headlong into the well, sunk into the womb of a beast; yet memory did not forsake me."

sanskrit: tvayā tu tārito 'smy adya kim anyatra tapobalāt anujānīhi māṃ kṛṣṇa gaccheyaṃ divam adya vai
english: "Today I have been ferried across by you—by what else than the power of austerity? Give me leave, O Kṛṣṇa, that I may go this very day to heaven."

sanskrit: anujñātaḥ sa kṛṣṇena namaskṛtya janārdanam vimānaṃ divyam āsthāya yayau divam ariṃdama
english: Granted leave by Kṛṣṇa, having bowed to Janārdana, he mounted a celestial chariot and went to heaven, O subduer of foes.

sanskrit: tatas tasmin divaṃ prāpte nṛge bharatasattama vāsudeva imaṃ ślokaṃ jagāda kurunandana
english: Then, when Nṛga had reached heaven, O best of the Bhāratas, Vāsudeva uttered this verse, O joy of the Kurus:

sanskrit: brāhmaṇasvaṃ na hartavyaṃ puruṣeṇa vijānatā brāhmaṇasvaṃ hṛtaṃ hanti nṛgaṃ brāhmaṇagaur iva
english: "A discerning man must never seize a brāhmaṇa's property; a brāhmaṇa's property, once seized, destroys, as the brāhmaṇa's cow destroyed Nṛga."

sanskrit: satāṃ samāgamaḥ sadbhir nāphalaḥ pārtha vidyate vimuktaṃ narakāt paśya nṛgaṃ sādhusamāgamāt
english: "Communion with the good, O Pārtha, is never fruitless for the good: behold how Nṛga was released from hell through fellowship with the holy."

sanskrit: pradānaṃ phalavat tatra drohas tatra tathāphalaḥ apacāraṃ gavāṃ tasmād varjayeta yudhiṣṭhira
english: "In this matter giving bears fruit, and so too does wrongdoing bear its fruit; therefore, Yudhiṣṭhira, one should shun any offence against cows."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca dattānāṃ phalasaṃprāptiṃ gavāṃ prabrūhi me 'nagha vistareṇa mahābāho na hi tṛpyāmi kathyatām
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Tell me, O sinless one, of the fruit that comes from cows that are given away; tell it at length, O mighty-armed—let it be told, for I am not yet sated.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam ṛṣer uddālaker vākyaṃ nāciketasya cobhayoḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: On this too they recount an ancient tale, the words of both the seer Uddālaka and of Nāciketa.

sanskrit: ṛṣir uddālakir dīkṣām upagamya tataḥ sutam tvaṃ mām upacarasveti nāciketam abhāṣata samāpte niyame tasmin maharṣiḥ putram abravīt
english: The seer Uddālaka, having undertaken a consecration, said to his son Nāciketa, "Attend upon me"; and when that observance was completed, the great seer spoke to his son.

sanskrit: upasparśanasaktasya svādhyāyaniratasya ca idhmā darbhāḥ sumanasaḥ kalaśaś cābhito jalam vismṛtaṃ me tad ādāya nadītīrād ihāvraja
english: "While I was intent on my ablutions and absorbed in my recitation, I forgot the kindling, the darbha grass, the flowers, the water-pot, and the water all about. Fetch them and come here from the riverbank."

sanskrit: gatvānavāpya tat sarvaṃ nadīvegasamāplutam na paśyāmi tad ity evaṃ pitaraṃ so 'bravīn muniḥ
english: Going there, the young ascetic could not recover any of it, for it had been swept away by the river's current; and so he said to his father, "I do not see it."

sanskrit: kṣutpipāsāśramāviṣṭo munir uddālakis tadā yamaṃ paśyeti taṃ putram aśapat sa mahātapāḥ
english: Then the sage Uddālaka, overcome by hunger, thirst, and weariness—he of great austerity—cursed his son, saying, "Go behold Yama!"

sanskrit: tathā sa pitrābhihato vāgvajreṇa kṛtāñjaliḥ prasīdeti bruvann eva gatasattvo 'patad bhuvi
english: Struck thus by his father with the thunderbolt of speech, with hands joined and saying only "Be gracious," the boy fell to the ground, his life gone out of him.

sanskrit: nāciketaṃ pitā dṛṣṭvā patitaṃ duḥkhamūrchitaḥ kiṃ mayā kṛtam ity uktvā nipapāta mahītale
english: Seeing Nāciketa fallen, the father, swooning with grief and crying, "What have I done!", sank down upon the earth.

sanskrit: tasya duḥkhaparītasya svaṃ putram upagūhataḥ vyatītaṃ tad ahaḥśeṣaṃ sā cogrā tatra śarvarī
english: For him, encompassed by sorrow as he held his own son in his embrace, the remainder of that day passed, and a grim night came over him there.

sanskrit: pitryeṇāśruprapātena nāciketaḥ kurūdvaha prāspandacchayane kauśye vṛṣṭyā sasyam ivāplutam
english: By the falling of his father's tears, O foremost of the Kurus, Nāciketa stirred upon the bed of kuśa grass, like a crop revived when steeped in rain.

sanskrit: sa paryapṛcchat taṃ putraṃ ślāghyaṃ pratyāgataṃ punaḥ divyair gandhaiḥ samādigdhaṃ kṣīṇasvapnam ivotthitam
english: He questioned that worthy son returned to him once more, anointed with celestial fragrances, risen as if from a fading dream.

sanskrit: api putra jitā lokāḥ śubhās te svena karmaṇā diṣṭyā cāsi punaḥ prāpto na hi te mānuṣaṃ vapuḥ
english: "Have you, my son, won the blessed worlds by your own deeds? By good fortune you are restored to me again—surely your form is no longer that of a mortal."

sanskrit: pratyakṣadarśī sarvasya pitrā pṛṣṭo mahātmanā anvarthaṃ taṃ pitur madhye maharṣīṇāṃ nyavedayat
english: He who had beheld all with his own eyes, when questioned by his great-souled father, recounted it truthfully to that father in the midst of the great seers.

sanskrit: kurvan bhavacchāsanam āśu yāto; hy ahaṃ viśālāṃ ruciraprabhāvām vaivasvatīṃ prāpya sabhām apaśyaṃ; sahasraśo yojanahaimabhaumām
english: "Carrying out your command, I went swiftly forth, and reaching the vast and radiantly lustrous hall of Vaivasvata, I beheld it, its golden floor stretching for thousands of leagues."

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvaiva mām abhimukham āpatantaṃ; gṛhaṃ nivedyāsanam ādideśa vaivasvato 'rghyādibhir arhaṇaiś ca; bhavatkṛte pūjayām āsa māṃ saḥ
english: "The moment he saw me hastening toward him, the son of Vivasvat showed me to his abode and assigned me a seat; and for your sake he honoured me with the welcome-offering and other tokens of reverence."

sanskrit: tatas tv ahaṃ taṃ śanakair avocaṃ; vṛtaṃ sadasyair abhipūjyamānam prāpto 'smi te viṣayaṃ dharmarāja; lokān arhe yān sma tān me vidhatsva
english: "Then softly I said to him, surrounded by his assessors and receiving their homage: 'O King of Dharma, I have come into your realm; ordain for me those worlds which I deserve.'"

sanskrit: yamo 'bravīn māṃ na mṛto 'si saumya; yamaṃ paśyety āha tu tvāṃ tapasvī pitā pradīptāgnisamānatejā; na tac chakyam anṛtaṃ vipra kartum
english: "Yama said to me: 'You are not dead, gentle one; yet your father the ascetic, in splendour like a blazing fire, bade you behold Yama—and that, O brāhmaṇa, cannot be made false.'"

sanskrit: dṛṣṭas te 'haṃ pratigacchasva tāta; śocaty asau tava dehasya kartā dadāmi kiṃ cāpi manaḥpraṇītaṃ; priyātithe tava kāmān vṛṇīṣva
english: "'You have beheld me—go back, my child; he who gave you your body is grieving. And I grant whatever your heart desires: choose your wishes, O welcome guest.'"

sanskrit: tenaivam uktas tam ahaṃ pratyavocaṃ; prāpto 'smi te viṣayaṃ durnivartyam icchāmy ahaṃ puṇyakṛtāṃ samṛddhāṃl; lokān draṣṭuṃ yadi te 'haṃ varārhaḥ
english: "Thus addressed by him, I answered him: 'I have reached your realm, hard to come back from; I wish to behold the abounding worlds of those who have done good, if I am worthy of a boon from you.'"

sanskrit: yānaṃ samāropya tu māṃ sa devo; vāhair yuktaṃ suprabhaṃ bhānumantam saṃdarśayām āsa tadā sma lokān; sarvāṃs tadā puṇyakṛtāṃ dvijendra
english: "Then that god, setting me upon a radiant, sun-bright chariot yoked with steeds, showed me at that time all the worlds of those who have done good, O foremost of brāhmaṇas."

sanskrit: apaśyaṃ tatra veśmāni taijasāni kṛtātmanām nānāsaṃsthānarūpāṇi sarvaratnamayāni ca
english: "There I beheld the gleaming mansions of the disciplined souls, of manifold shapes and forms and wrought all of jewels."

sanskrit: candramaṇḍalaśubhrāṇi kiṅkiṇījālavanti ca anekaśatabhaumāni sāntarjalavanāni ca
english: "White as the disc of the moon, festooned with networks of little bells, of many hundred storeys, set amid waters and groves within."

sanskrit: vaiḍūryārkaprakāśāni rūpyarukmamayāni ca taruṇādityavarṇāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca
english: "Shining like beryl and the sun, fashioned of silver and gold, of the hue of the young morning sun, some fixed and some that moved at will."

sanskrit: bhakṣyabhojyamayāñ śailān vāsāṃsi śayanāni ca sarvakāmaphalāṃś caiva vṛkṣān bhavanasaṃsthitān
english: "Mountains made of food hard and soft, and garments and couches, and trees bearing the fruit of every desire, standing about the dwellings."

sanskrit: nadyo vīthyaḥ sabhā vāpī dīrghikāś caiva sarvaśaḥ ghoṣavanti ca yānāni yuktāny eva sahasraśaḥ
english: "Rivers, avenues, assembly-halls, ponds, and long pools on every side, and chiming chariots ready-yoked by the thousand."

sanskrit: kṣīrasravā vai sarito girīṃś ca; sarpis tathā vimalaṃ cāpi toyam vaivasvatasyānumatāṃś ca deśān; adṛṣṭapūrvān subahūn apaśyam
english: "Rivers flowing with milk, and mountains, and clarified butter, and water utterly clear; many regions sanctioned by Vaivasvata, never seen before, did I behold."

sanskrit: sarvaṃ dṛṣṭvā tad ahaṃ dharmarājam; avocaṃ vai prabhaviṣṇuṃ purāṇam kṣīrasyaitāḥ sarpiṣaś caiva nadyaḥ; śaśvat srotāḥ kasya bhojyāḥ pradiṣṭāḥ
english: "Having seen all this, I said to the King of Dharma, the ancient and almighty one: 'These rivers of milk and of clarified butter, ever-flowing—for whose enjoyment are they ordained?'"

sanskrit: yamo 'bravīd viddhi bhojyās tvam etā; ye dātāraḥ sādhavo gorasānām anye lokāḥ śāśvatā vītaśokāḥ; samākīrṇā gopradāne ratānām
english: "Yama said: 'Know that these are to be enjoyed by those good men who are givers of the products of the cow; and there are still other worlds, eternal and free from sorrow, thronged with those devoted to the gift of cows.'"

sanskrit: na tv evāsāṃ dānamātraṃ praśastaṃ; pātraṃ kālo goviśeṣo vidhiś ca jñātvā deyā vipra gavāntaraṃ hi; duḥkhaṃ jñātuṃ pāvakādityabhūtam
english: "'Yet the mere giving of them is not what is praised; the worthy recipient, the time, the particular cow, and the rite all matter. Knowing these, O brāhmaṇa, should one give—for the true worth of a cow is as hard to discern as the nature of fire and the sun.'"

sanskrit: svādhyāyāḍhyo yo 'timātraṃ tapasvī; vaitānastho brāhmaṇaḥ pātram āsām kṛcchrotsṛṣṭāḥ poṣaṇābhyāgatāś ca; dvārair etair goviśeṣāḥ praśastāḥ
english: "'A brāhmaṇa rich in sacred recitation, exceedingly austere, established in the sacrificial fires, is the worthy recipient of these. Cows released in time of hardship, or come for their nurture—by such avenues are particular cows esteemed.'"

sanskrit: tisro rātrīr adbhir upoṣya bhūmau; tṛptā gāvas tarpitebhyaḥ pradeyāḥ vatsaiḥ prītāḥ suprajāḥ sopacārās; tryahaṃ dattvā gorasair vartitavyam
english: "'Having fasted three nights on water and lying on the bare ground, contented cows should be given to those who have been satisfied—cows glad with their calves, rich in offspring, attended with all due rites; and having given them, for three days one should live upon the cow's own products.'"

sanskrit: dattvā dhenuṃ suvratāṃ kāṃsyadohāṃ; kalyāṇavatsām apalāyinīṃ ca yāvanti lomāni bhavanti tasyās; tāvad varṣāṇy aśnute svargalokam
english: "'Having given a milch-cow of gentle ways, milked into bronze, with a fair calf and not given to straying—for as many hairs as are upon her, for so many years does the giver enjoy the world of heaven.'"

sanskrit: tathānaḍvāhaṃ brāhmaṇāya pradāya; dāntaṃ dhuryaṃ balavantaṃ yuvānam kulānujīvaṃ vīryavantaṃ bṛhantaṃ; bhuṅkte lokān saṃmitān dhenudasya
english: "'So too, having given to a brāhmaṇa an ox—tamed, fit for the yoke, strong and young, sustaining its lineage, vigorous and great—one enjoys worlds equal to those of the giver of a milch-cow.'"

sanskrit: goṣu kṣāntaṃ gośaraṇyaṃ kṛtajñaṃ; vṛttiglānaṃ tādṛśaṃ pātram āhuḥ vṛttiglāne saṃbhrame vā mahārthe; kṛṣyarthe vā homahetoḥ prasūtyām
english: "'One forbearing toward cows, a refuge to cows, grateful, and worn down in his livelihood—such a man they call a worthy recipient; whether in failing livelihood, in some great emergency, for the sake of ploughing, for an oblation, or at a birth—'"

sanskrit: gurvarthe vā bālapuṣṭyābhiṣaṅgād; gāvo dātuṃ deśakālo 'viśiṣṭaḥ antarjātāḥ sukrayajñānalabdhāḥ; prāṇakrītā nirjitāś caudakāś ca
english: "'—or for a teacher's sake, or out of concern for the nourishment of children: no particular place or time is required for giving cows. Such cows may be born among one's own herd, gained by fair purchase, acquired by sacrifice or knowledge, bought at the price of one's own life, won in battle, or received as a libation of water.'"

sanskrit: nāciketa uvāca śrutvā vaivasvatavacas tam ahaṃ punar abruvam agomī gopradātṝṇāṃ kathaṃ lokān nigacchati
english: Nāciketa said: "Having heard the words of Vaivasvata, I asked him again: 'How does one who has no cow attain the worlds of the givers of cows?'"

sanskrit: tato yamo 'bravīd dhīmān gopradāne parāṃ gatim gopradānānukalpaṃ tu gām ṛte santi gopradāḥ
english: "Then the wise Yama said: 'The gift of a cow leads to the highest goal; yet there are substitutes for the gift of a cow, and even without a cow there are those who count as cow-givers.'"

sanskrit: alābhe yo gavāṃ dadyād ghṛtadhenuṃ yatavrataḥ tasyaitā ghṛtavāhinyaḥ kṣarante vatsalā iva
english: "'He who, lacking cows, gives a cow made of clarified butter, firm in his vow—for him these rivers of butter flow as tenderly as loving cows yielding their milk.'"

sanskrit: ghṛtālābhe ca yo dadyāt tiladhenuṃ yatavrataḥ sa durgāt tārito dhenvā kṣīranadyāṃ pramodate
english: "'And he who, wanting butter, gives a cow made of sesame, firm in his vow, is borne across distress by that cow and rejoices in the river of milk.'"

sanskrit: tilālābhe ca yo dadyāj jaladhenuṃ yatavrataḥ sa kāmapravahāṃ śītāṃ nadīm etām upāśnute
english: "'And he who, wanting sesame, gives a cow made of water, firm in his vow, comes to enjoy this cool river that flows at his desire.'"

sanskrit: evamādīni me tatra dharmarājo nyadarśayat dṛṣṭvā ca paramaṃ harṣam avāpam aham acyuta
english: "Such things and more did the King of Dharma show me there; and beholding them I attained the highest joy, O Acyuta."

sanskrit: nivedaye cāpi priyaṃ bhavatsu; kratur mahān alpadhanapracāraḥ prāpto mayā tāta sa matprasūtaḥ; prapatsyate vedavidhipravṛttaḥ
english: "And I announce to you a glad tiding: a great sacrifice, requiring but small wealth to perform, has come to me, dear father, sprung from me; conducted by the rule of the Veda, it shall come to fruition."

sanskrit: śāpo hy ayaṃ bhavato 'nugrahāya; prāpto mayā yatra dṛṣṭo yamo me dānavyuṣṭiṃ tatra dṛṣṭvā mahārthāṃ; niḥsaṃdigdhaṃ dānadharmāṃś cariṣye
english: "For this curse of yours came to me as a grace, in which I beheld Yama; and having there seen the great reward of giving, I shall practise the duties of gift-giving beyond all doubt."

sanskrit: idaṃ ca mām abravīd dharmarājaḥ; punaḥ punaḥ saṃprahṛṣṭo dvijarṣe dānena tāta prayato 'bhūḥ sadaiva; viśeṣato gopradānaṃ ca kuryāḥ
english: "And this the King of Dharma told me again and again, greatly pleased, O seer among brāhmaṇas: 'Be ever assiduous in giving, my child, and above all perform the gift of cows.'"

sanskrit: śuddho hy artho nāvamanyaḥ svadharmāt; pātre deyaṃ deśakālopapanne tasmād gāvas te nityam eva pradeyā; mā bhūc ca te saṃśayaḥ kaś cid atra
english: "'For wealth honestly come by must not be scorned: in accord with your own duty, it should be given to a worthy recipient at a fitting place and time. Therefore cows should ever be given by you; let no doubt of any kind arise in you here.'"

sanskrit: etāḥ purā adadan nityam eva; śāntātmāno dānapathe niviṣṭāḥ tapāṃsy ugrāṇy apratiśaṅkamānās; te vai dānaṃ pradaduś cāpi śaktyā
english: "'These men of old, of tranquil soul, set upon the path of giving, gave cows unceasingly; undertaking fierce austerities without misgiving, they too bestowed gifts to the full measure of their power.'"

sanskrit: kāle śaktyā matsaraṃ varjayitvā; śuddhātmānaḥ śraddhinaḥ puṇyaśīlāḥ dattvā taptvā lokam amuṃ prapannā; dedīpyante puṇyaśīlāś ca nāke
english: "'Giving in due time according to their power, casting envy aside—pure of soul, faithful, of virtuous conduct—having given and having done penance, they have attained yonder world, and these men of virtuous conduct shine resplendent in heaven.'"

sanskrit: etad dānaṃ nyāyalabdhaṃ dvijebhyaḥ; pātre dattaṃ prāpaṇīyaṃ parīkṣya kāmyāṣṭamyāṃ vartitavyaṃ daśāhaṃ; rasair gavāṃ śakṛtā prasnavair vā
english: "'This gift, won by lawful means and given to brāhmaṇas, should be conferred upon a worthy recipient after due scrutiny; and on the desired eighth day one should pass ten days living on the products of the cow—its milk, its dung, or its yield.'"

sanskrit: vedavratī syād vṛṣabhapradātā; vedāvāptir goyugasya pradāne tīrthāvāptir goprayuktapradāne; pāpotsargaḥ kapilāyāḥ pradāne
english: "'The giver of a bull keeps the vow of the Veda; the gift of a yoke of cattle yields the attainment of the Veda; the gift of a yoked team yields the attainment of holy fords; and the gift of a tawny cow yields the casting-off of sin.'"

sanskrit: gām apy ekāṃ kapilāṃ saṃpradāya; nyāyopetāṃ kalmaṣād vipramucyet gavāṃ rasāt paramaṃ nāsti kiṃ cid; gavāṃ dānaṃ sumahat tad vadanti
english: "'By bestowing even a single tawny cow, lawfully come by, one is wholly freed from defilement. Than the milk of cows there is nothing higher; the gift of cows, they declare, is a very great thing.'"

sanskrit: gāvo lokān dhārayanti kṣarantyo; gāvaś cānnaṃ saṃjanayanti loke yas taj jānan na gavāṃ hārdam eti; sa vai gantā nirayaṃ pāpacetāḥ
english: "'Cows, yielding their milk, sustain the worlds; cows bring forth food in the world. The man who, knowing this, does not give his heart to cows—that man of evil mind shall surely go to hell.'"

sanskrit: yat te dātuṃ gosahasraṃ śataṃ vā; śatārdhaṃ vā daśa vā sādhuvatsāḥ apy ekāṃ vā sādhave brāhmaṇāya; sāsyāmuṣmin puṇyatīrthā nadī vai
english: "'Whether you have a thousand cows to give, or a hundred, or fifty, or ten with goodly calves, or even one to a worthy brāhmaṇa—she shall be for that man a river of holy fords in the world beyond.'"

sanskrit: prāptyā puṣṭyā lokasaṃrakṣaṇena; gāvas tulyāḥ sūryapādaiḥ pṛthivyām śabdaś caikaḥ saṃtatiś copabhogas; tasmād godaḥ sūrya ivābhibhāti
english: "'In their bounty, their nourishment, and their guarding of the world, cows on earth are the equals of the sun's rays: the name is the same, the lineage is the same, and the enjoyment is the same; therefore the giver of cows shines forth like the sun.'"

sanskrit: guruṃ śiṣyo varayed gopradāne; sa vai vaktā niyataṃ svargadātā vidhijñānāṃ sumahān eṣa dharmo; vidhiṃ hy ādyaṃ vidhayaḥ saṃśrayanti
english: "'In the gift of cows the disciple should choose a teacher; he, the reciter of the rite, is assuredly the bestower of heaven. Great among those who know the rites is this duty; for all rites have recourse to that first ordinance.'"

sanskrit: etad dānaṃ nyāyalabdhaṃ dvijebhyaḥ; pātre dattvā prāpayethāḥ parīkṣya tvayy āśaṃsanty amarā mānavāś ca; vayaṃ cāpi prasṛte puṇyaśīlāḥ
english: "'This gift, won by lawful means, you should confer upon brāhmaṇas, giving it to a worthy recipient after due scrutiny. Upon you the immortals and men alike set their hopes, and we too, men of virtuous conduct, when the gift goes forth.'"

sanskrit: ity ukto 'haṃ dharmarājñā maharṣe; dharmātmānaṃ śirasābhipraṇamya anujñātas tena vaivasvatena; pratyāgamaṃ bhagavatpādamūlam
english: "Thus addressed by the King of Dharma, O great seer, bowing my head to that righteous one, and given leave by Vaivasvata, I came back to the feet of your reverence."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca uktaṃ vai gopradānaṃ te nāciketam ṛṣiṃ prati māhātmyam api caivoktam uddeśena gavāṃ prabho
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: You have spoken of the gift of cows in connection with the seer Nāciketa, and you have also told, by way of summary, the greatness of cows, O lord.

sanskrit: nṛgeṇa ca yathā duḥkham anubhūtaṃ mahātmanā ekāparādhād ajñānāt pitāmaha mahāmate
english: And how the great-souled Nṛga underwent suffering through a single offence committed in ignorance, O grandsire of mighty mind;

sanskrit: dvāravatyāṃ yathā cāsau niviśantyāṃ samuddhṛtaḥ mokṣahetur abhūt kṛṣṇas tad apy avadhṛtaṃ mayā
english: and how he was raised up at Dvāravatī while it was being settled, Kṛṣṇa becoming the cause of his deliverance—this too I have grasped.

sanskrit: kiṃ tv asti mama saṃdeho gavāṃ lokaṃ prati prabho tattvataḥ śrotum icchāmi godā yatra viśanty uta
english: But a doubt remains in me concerning the world of cows, O lord; I wish to hear truly into what region the givers of cows enter.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam yathāpṛcchat padmayonim etad eva śatakratuḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: On this too they recount an ancient tale, how Śatakratu put this very question to the Lotus-born.

sanskrit: śakra uvāca svarlokavāsināṃ lakṣmīm abhibhūya svayā tviṣā golokavāsinaḥ paśye vrajataḥ saṃśayo 'tra me
english: Śakra said: Outshining by their own radiance the splendour of those who dwell in heaven, I behold the dwellers of the cow-world faring on; herein lies my doubt.

sanskrit: kīdṛśā bhagavaṃl lokā gavāṃ tad brūhi me 'nagha yān āvasanti dātāra etad icchāmi veditum
english: Of what nature, O blessed one, are the worlds of cows? Tell me that, O sinless one—those that the givers inhabit; this I wish to know.

sanskrit: kīdṛśāḥ kiṃphalāḥ kaḥ svit paramas tatra vai guṇaḥ kathaṃ ca puruṣās tatra gacchanti vigatajvarāḥ
english: Of what kind are they, what fruit do they bear, and what is the supreme excellence there? And how do men come thither, freed from all affliction?

sanskrit: kiyat kālaṃ pradānasya dātā ca phalam aśnute kathaṃ bahuvidhaṃ dānaṃ syād alpam api vā katham
english: For how long does the giver enjoy the fruit of his gift? And how is a gift made manifold, or how even a small one?

sanskrit: bahvīnāṃ kīdṛśaṃ dānam alpānāṃ vāpi kīdṛśam adattvā gopradāḥ santi kena vā tac ca śaṃsa me
english: What is the giving of many cows like, and what the giving of few? And by what means are there those reckoned cow-givers who have given none? Tell me that as well.

sanskrit: kathaṃ ca bahudātā syād alpadātrā samaḥ prabho alpapradātā bahudaḥ kathaṃ ca syād iheśvara
english: And how may the giver of many be the equal of the giver of few, O lord? And how may the giver of little rank as a giver of much, O master here?

sanskrit: kīdṛśī dakṣiṇā caiva gopradāne viśiṣyate etat tathyena bhagavan mama śaṃsitum arhasi
english: And what kind of sacrificial fee is esteemed highest in the gift of cows? All this, O blessed one, you ought to declare to me in truth.

sanskrit: brahmovāca yo 'yaṃ praśnas tvayā pṛṣṭo gopradānādhikāravān nāsya praṣṭāsti loke 'smiṃs tvatto 'nyo hi śatakrato
english: Brahmā said: This question that you have asked, bearing upon the worthiness for the gift of cows—there is in this world no questioner of it other than you, O Śatakratu.
